Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 05-Jan-2026 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - DEC 2025 / JAN 2026  
  SUBJECT: ICT 3123/IT_3123 SOFTWARE ENGINEERING  
  (SPL: INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY)  
  SOFTWARE ENGINEERING [ICT 3123]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)                Design a sequence diagram for an Online Banking System where a customer transfers money from (5)  
  their savings account to a friend's checking account.  
  The system must:  
  
  Validate login credentials and send an SMS code for second-step verification (one retry  
  allowed before temporary account lock and security alert).  
  Upon successful authentication, verify sufficient balance in the savings account.  
  If funds are available, initiate the transfer by communicating concurrently with the Payment  
  Processing Network (external) and the Transaction Logger (internal). The system should  
  remain responsive during network delays.  
  After payment confirmation, record the transaction, update both accounts, destroy  
  temporary tokens, and send email/SMS notifications to both parties.  
  
  Explain your design choices regarding flow control, conditional paths, and communication patterns  
  used.  
1B)                A banking software system has been designed with the following module interactions: Module A         (3)  
  passes an account number (integer) to Module B for balance verification. Module C receives a  
  customer data structure from Module D, but only uses the customer's credit score field. Module E  
  sends a flag to Module F that determines whether to execute loan approval or rejection logic within  
  Module F. Module G and Module H both access a global variable containing current interest rates.  
  Module I directly modifies internal data variables of Module J and uses goto statements to jump into  
  Module J's processing logic. Analyze each interaction by identifying the specific type of coupling  
  present and rank them from most desirable to least desirable. Explain why the ranking you propose  
  aligns with software engineering principles for maintainable system design.  
1C)                In what scenarios would you recommend using a hybrid integration testing approach over a top-          (2)  
  down or bottom-up approach? Explain your reasoning.  
2A)                Analyze the merits and demerits of Client/Server Style, Repository Style, and Layered System.          (5)  
  Synthesize a Hybrid Architecture Solution using these three styles for a distributed e-commerce  
  system that must handle high traffic, ensure data consistency, and provide real-time inventory  
  updates across multiple geographic regions.  
2B)                A simple digital watch has a display and two buttons to set it, the A button and the B button. The  (3)  
  watch has two modes of operation, display time and set time. In the display time mode, the watch  
  displays hours and minutes, separated by a flashing colon. The set time mode has two submodes,  
  set hours and set minutes. The A button selects modes. Each time it is pressed, the mode  
  advances in the sequence: display, set hours, set minutes, display, etc. Within the submodes, the B  
  button advances the hours or minutes once each time it is pressed. Buttons must be released  
  before they can generate another event. Prepare a state diagram of the watch.  
  
  Page #1

2C)            A software development team has created a module that handles user authentication, generates          (2)  
  system logs, sends email notifications, and validates input data formats. When asked to justify their  
  design, they argue that these functions are logically related because they all support the main  
  application functionality. Analyze this design decision by identifying the type of cohesion currently  
  present and propose a restructured design that would better align with software engineering best  
  practices.  
3A)            Design the test cases for the following code snippet using path testing. You are expected to follow   (5)  
  the following steps to design an effective test case which have a high probability of revealing  
  defects.  
  
  1. Draw the CFG (Control Flow Graph)  
  2. Find the Cyclomatic Complexity using three methods.  
  3. Identify the independent paths (Basic Path Set)  
  4. Derive test cases  
  
  int main()  
  {  
  int percentage;  
  char grade;  
  do {  
  printf("Enter an percentage :");  
  scanf("%d", &percentage);  
  
  $$if (percentage >=90)$$  
  $$grade='A';$$  
  $$else if (percentage >=80)$$  
  $$grade='B';$$  
  $$else if (percentage >=70)$$  
  $$grade='C';$$  
  $$else if (percentage >=60)$$  
  $$grade='D';$$  
  $$else if (percentage >=50)$$  
  $$grade='E';$$  
  else  
  $$grade = 'U';$$  
  
  printf("nnWant to check again (press Y/y for 'yes') :");  
  scanf(" %c", &choice);  
  $$} while (choice == 'Y' || choice == 'y');$$  
  
  printf("nYour grade is %c", grade);  
  
  return 0;  
  }  
3B)            A software development project has identified the following risks: 30% probability that a key team (3)  
  member will leave (impact cost: \$15,000), 60% probability of requirement changes causing delays  
  (impact cost: \$8,000), and 20% probability of integration issues with third-party systems (impact  
  cost: \$25,000). The project manager must decide between reactive and proactive risk management  
  approaches. Calculate the risk exposure for each identified risk using the Risk Exposure formula,  
  categorize these risks according to the material's classification approaches, and develop an  
  appropriate Risk Mitigation, Monitoring, and Management (RMMM) strategy for the highest priority  
  risk. Justify whether a proactive or reactive approach would be more suitable for this project  
  scenario.  
3C)            Discuss the key phases of Requirements Engineering and analyze how each phase contributes to          (2)  
  the success of a software project.  
4A)   Based on the shipping cost calculator interface shown in Figure 4(A), design a comprehensive test plan for the       (5)  
  calculateShippingCost(weight, zone) function using Equivalence Class Partitioning technique. Your test plan  
  should include:  
  
  Page #2

a) Identify all valid and invalid equivalence classes for both input parameters (weight and destination zone)  
  b) Create test cases that cover each equivalence class  
  c) Specify expected results for each test case  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
4B)            A university library provides services to students and faculty. Users can search for books, borrow  (3)  
  books, and return books. A librarian manages the catalog and updates book records. The system  
  also sends due-date reminders to users. Construct a use-case model for this Library Management  
  System. Also, create an Activity Diagram for the process of Updating Book Records by the librarian.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
4C)            Analyze the advantages and disadvantages of using Extreme Programming (XP) in a large                  (2)  
  organization compared to a small startup.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5A)            Create a class diagram for the following specification: Each instructor can teach several courses,     (5)  
  Page #3

and each course may be taught by more than one instructor. A student may register for many  
  courses, and each course can have many students. A course is assigned to exactly one classroom,  
  but a classroom may host different courses at different times. Each instructor is responsible for  
  guiding multiple students, and a student may be guided by exactly one instructor. Draw the UML  
  class diagram for this specification. Also, analyze whether the use of association class is possible  
  with the relationship between Students and Courses. If yes, illustrate with a revised class diagram  
  justifying such association class. If not, specify the reason.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
5B)                   Analyze the general features and content of Software Configuration Management (SCM) and                  (3)  
  discuss its significance in maintaining project integrity and facilitating collaborative development.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5C)                   Compare verification and validation in the V-software process model, analyzing how each                  (2)  
  contributes to the quality of the software product.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"
